correctness.rationale: The spanning-tree probability of containing edge set F is the determinant of the unit-conductance transfer-current kernel K_F, obtained by differentiating the matrix-tree polynomial. Explicit solution of the K(a,b) Laplacian gives K_(uv,u'v')=1_(u=u')/b+1_(v=v')/a-1/(ab), diagonal p=(a+b-1)/(ab). Hadamard bounds arbitrary r-edge inclusion by p^r; a disjoint r-matching has exact probability q_r=(a+b)^(r-1)(a+b-r)/(ab)^r. Independence of k trees gives EX=ab p^k and exact second factorial moment. Negative pair dependence yields Var X<=EX, proving the supercritical nonempty event; factorial moment sandwiches for b/a^(k-1)->theta give all Poisson moments and dominated factorial inversion proves TV convergence. Overlap collision estimates and S_a×S_b symmetry prove asymptotic uniform bipartite matching edge set. Independent exact small K(a,b) tree enumeration checked determinants, pair moments and matching formulas, not asymptotic truth.
residual_risks: The threshold holds for fixed k>=3 with a->infty, b>=a; not k growing or fixed smaller part.
